geometry_edits.rationale: Recast the dominant mass as a hall section rather than a generic stepped object so the roof/section can express span and daylight.
Use the portfolio-preferred section family to introduce a clear daylighting roof logic compatible with a gymnasium.
Align the hall section with the long axis so the visible mass reads as a long-span gym body rather than a square object.
Introduce a carved public void to address the access edge and create a legible ground threshold.
Keep the void bounded so it behaves like a public court/entry carve rather than hollowing the entire mass.
Open the public void toward the access-aligned side in the program frame to repair the sealed frontage condition.
Make the courtyard the new root so the hall remains in ancestry while the public threshold becomes primary.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the arbitrary stepped mass with a more legible step-envelope that can be re-authored as a hall-like datum while preserving the dominant linear bar gesture.
Reduce excessive tiering so the mass reads less like a cake stack and more like a compact hall with one dominant datum.
Tighten the step depth to keep continuity in the main mass and avoid over-fragmented terrace bands.
Minimize lateral drift so the stepped section reads as one continuous hall volume instead of a staggered stack.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent stepped bar in all four views and the geometry is not visibly self-colliding, so repair integrity is good. However, the dominant gesture reads as a generic stacked pyramid/terraced object rather than a clear long-span gymnasium hall. The section is too compressed and repetitive for the program contract: there is no convincing roof/span/daylight logic, no subordinate service/entry bar, and no legible public threshold responding to the verified access edge. The blue access edge is not meaningfully opened by a court, undercut, seam, or entry carve; the mass mostly seals the parcel rather than organizing a public ground condition. The form resonates somewhat with sports-architecture references through its compactness and horizontal base, but its stepped silhouette is closer to an abstract object than an inhabitable hall. Because the visible mass does not plausibly support the gymnasium semantic invariants, program_fit_hard_pass fails.
